methodological_rigor.justification: The study combines TCGA-HNSC bioinformatics, 73 paired OSCC/adjacent tissue TMA with blinded IHC scoring by two observers, three OSCC cell lines (SAS, SCC25, HSC-3), siRNA knockdown plus plasmid overexpression of Gal-1, Ferrostatin-1 rescue, lipid ROS quantification, Western blot, qPCR, and an SAS xenograft (n=5/group NOD-SCID) with TPL at 0.15 mg/kg/day for 14 days. Strengths include rescue experiments and Fer-1 specificity testing. Limitations: most mechanistic work in SAS with HSC-3 only partial validation, single dose in vivo, no iron chelation or GPX4 overexpression rescue, ferroptosis inferred from a narrow marker set, and authors acknowledge this. Statistical analysis relies on unpaired two-tailed t-test even for multi-group comparisons where ANOVA would be more appropriate; no power calculation; no multiplicity correction.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study combining cell lines, xenografts, and retrospective tissue correlation, mapping to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is plausible: TPL is a compound with prior OSCC in vivo efficacy data (ref 17 from same group), the Gal-1 prognostic association is validated in TCGA and local 73-patient cohort (T-category and AJCC stage significance), and the ferroptosis framework is therapeutically actionable. Translational path to clinic requires considerable additional work.

reporting_quality.justification: Animal work reports IACUC approval number, randomization to groups, blinding of IHC observers, and euthanasia/sampling details, partially aligning with ARRIVE 2.0. Essential 10 items not fully addressed (no sample-size justification, no reporting of exclusions, limited blinding of in-vitro experiments). IHC scoring methodology is clearly detailed and blinded. Primer sequences, antibody catalog numbers, and cell-line sources are reported. No data or code deposition statement; raw images not made available.

novelty_literature.justification: Triptolide-induced ferroptosis has been previously reported in cervical cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma (refs 9, 10), and Galectin-1's role in sorafenib-resistance-linked ferroptosis in HCC was shown by Hsu et al. (ref 13). The novel contribution is extending this axis specifically to OSCC, demonstrating Gal-1 modulation of GPX4/SLC7A11/FTH1 in OSCC, and showing partial rescue of TPL effects by Gal-1 restoration. This is a meaningful incremental extension rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally clear, logically organized, and appropriately hedged (explicit acknowledgment of limitations and alternative interpretations). Figures are described with sufficient detail. Minor issues: repeated phrases ('dissolved in dissolved in'), a reference to 'reviewer feedback' that should not appear in a final manuscript, and occasional redundancy between conclusion and discussion sections. Writing quality is adequate for publication after minor editing.

key_strengths: Integrated in silico (TCGA), clinical (73 paired OSCC TMA), in vitro (three cell lines), genetic (siRNA + overexpression), pharmacological (Fer-1 rescue), and in vivo (xenograft) evidence for a Gal-1-ferroptosis axis
Blinded dual-observer IHC scoring of the patient cohort with clinicopathological correlation
Explicit Fer-1 rescue supporting ferroptosis specificity of TPL effect
Clear Gal-1 prognostic validation in TCGA and local cohort
key_concerns: Ferroptosis inferred from a narrow marker panel (GPX4, lipid ROS); no iron chelation or GPX4 rescue to confirm causality
Most mechanistic experiments performed only in SAS; HSC-3 validation limited and SCC25 not fully used
Statistical analyses rely on t-test for multi-group comparisons; no multiplicity correction
Retained editorial artifact ('reviewer feedback' reference) and typographical error ('dissolved in dissolved in')
No new-data or code deposition statement; single in vivo dose and schedule
Novelty incremental relative to published TPL-ferroptosis and Gal-1-ferroptosis work in other tumors
chief_reviewer.rationale: Mechanistically coherent OSCC ferroptosis study with respectable multi-modality validation but incremental novelty, limited ferroptosis marker breadth, and residual editing issues; appropriate for a tier-3 oncology or head-and-neck specialty journal after major revisions.
